Events inside the window: (1) the 35M-share ATM/collared-forward program [5] and weekly 10b5-1-style insider sales (CEO filing Form 144s for 200k shares a week, ~$275M of notices since Aug 12 [6]). This is steady supply overhang, a mild negative. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 earnings in late October (MSFT/META/GOOGL/AMZN) with 2027 capex commentary. This is the main two-sided event for AI-infra sentiment. (3) FOMC late October and macro prints. (4) Momentum is mixed: -25% in the month to Sep 17, then a rebound from $79.88 to $88.57 [10]. My ladder is close to symmetric around a slightly lower median ($87.8) at the stock's usual monthly vol (93%/3.5 ~= 26%), with only a small tilt for dilution supply.

fair_value.method: Blend of a vintage-based unlevered DCF ($45/share: revenue/capex 0.42, 60% EBITDA margin, 6-yr life + 3-yr 50% residual, WACC 11.5%, g 3%, ~$67B net debt at Oct-2027, 620M shares) and 5.5x NTM EBITDA of $20.9B ($78/share), weighted 50/50. The DCF is extremely sensitive: plausible input changes swing it from about -$50 to +$108.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: 35-yr vintage model as of 2027-10-01: 2027 rev $22.7B, 2028 $39.5B, 2030 $69.9B; EBITDA margin 60%; capex $45/45/40/35B for 2027-30; FCF -$31.5B (2027), -$21.6B (2028), turns positive in 2030; WACC 11.5%; g 3%; EV $94B less net debt $66.6B = equity $27.7B / 620M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Exit ARR midpoint $19B used as the revenue of the installed fleet at end-2026.

Installed fleet $19B ARR rolling off over ~4.5 yrs plus 2027 deployments; 41% of $103.7B RPO falls in the 24 months to Jun-2028 (~$21B/yr) per 10-Q; deliberately ~14% below the $26.37B consensus to reflect the delivery delays that triggered JPM/Macquarie cuts.

Observed: Q2 annualised revenue $10.3B vs ~$38B average in-service gross PP&E ~= 0.27-0.30 (PP&E $46.7B incl. $11.9B CIP). Adjusted up for the ~25% July price increase and the 5-10pp higher contribution margin on new contracts the CFO cited. Sensitivity: 0.36 -> about -$50/share, 0.44 -> about +$76/share.

Cost of equity 14.7% = 10Y UST 5.24% + beta ~1.9 x 5% ERP (beta judged from 93% realised vol). Pre-tax debt cost 9.5% (unsecured coupons 8.5-9.75%, secondary yields 11.4-12.1%; converts 1.75-2.875%), 7.5% after tax. Weights 56/44 on $48.8B market cap vs ~$38B net debt. 10.5% -> $75, 12.5% -> $22.
Below the nominal 10Y yield; GPU-cloud capacity is treated as a mature utility-like service after 2060 in the 35-yr explicit model.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 5.5x NTM EBITDA $20.9B = EV $115B less net debt $66.6B = $48.3B / 620M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x 2027E $13.5B + 0.75 x 2028E $23.4B from the DCF revenue/margin model.

PV of a 6-year EBITDA annuity at 11.5% is 4.2x, plus the residual-period value (~0.5x), gives 4.7x for installed assets; a modest growth premium gets to 5.5x. The market today is ~7.5x NTM (EV ~$86B = $48.8B cap + ~$38B net debt on ~$11.6B NTM EBITDA). The skeptic view is that the multiple compresses as refinancing and dilution continue.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or a customer stumble (top 3 customers = 72% of revenue [2]) meets a funding wall. 2027 needs ~$30B+ of external capital at 9-12% yields [8]. CDS is back above 850bp [7], equity is issued below $60, and re-contracted Hopper pricing disappoints. The market starts valuing equity as a thin sliver over ~$60B+ net debt.

base.story: Backlog converts roughly on schedule ($129B incl. Q3 adds [7]) and margins reach low teens in adj. operating terms [3]. But 2027 FCF is about -$30B, funded by continued convert/ATM/DDTL issuance, so per-share value is diluted and the EV/EBITDA multiple drifts down toward 6-7x. The stock ends roughly flat to modestly lower.

bull.story: Pricing power persists (July +25% price increase, B200 rental rates up strongly [21][3]) and re-contracting of old fleets proves very profitable. Delivery accelerates toward >3 GW by end-2027 and credit spreads compress (as in H1-2026 [22]). The stock re-rates toward the $141 consensus target [18].

thesis_break_reason: Below the $60.55 52-week low, the equity (~$34B at 620M shares) would be worth roughly half of projected 2027 net debt. Trading there would most likely mean credit markets are refusing to fund the capex plan on acceptable terms (CDS/bond blowout, a failed or heavily discounted raise), a major customer has delayed or cut commitments, or GPU re-contracting economics have broken. Any of these is a fundamental impairment, not ordinary volatility for a 93%-vol stock.

key_uncertainties: True economic life of GPUs and the price of re-contracted capacity. This is the single largest DCF driver (5 vs 7 years swings value by >$130/share).
Revenue yield per $ of capex. Observed ~0.3; needs to be ~0.4+ for the growth capex to clear an 11.5% WACC.
Access to and cost of capital for ~$30B+ of annual external funding. CDS ran 810-855bp in 2026.
Customer concentration (72% of Q2 revenue from top 3) and counterparty credit of AI-lab customers.
Dilution path (ATM, converts at $97.85/$119.60 strikes, SBC) vs share count assumptions.
Whether AI infrastructure demand stays supply-constrained through 2027. Firm GPU rental indices argue it does for now.
reasoning: Skeptic lane. I used primary filings and credit/insider data to check whether the consensus (avg PT $141.58, 28 of 41 Buy) is too optimistic. The hard facts: Q2 revenue was $2.58B (+112%) with 59% adj. EBITDA margin, but net loss was -$626M, interest expense $640M (guided to $860-940M for Q3), cash FCF -$5.7B, and accrual capex $9.4B. Debt was $35.1B at Jun-30, plus a $4.2B convert in September, plus a 35M-share ATM. Total liabilities are $72B against $5B of equity. Insiders filed ~$275M of Form 144 notices in seven weeks. CDS reached 810-855bp. Ratings are Ba3/B+. A securities class action is pending. The key skeptic finding is unit economics. On observed data, revenue per $ of in-service PP&E is only ~0.27-0.30, and at 59% margin that gives an unlevered cash yield (~17%/yr) that barely recovers capex over a 6-year life. My DCF therefore hinges on price increases (+25% in July), higher new-contract margins and residual value from re-contracting. With generous-but-defensible inputs (0.42 yield, 60% margin, 6+3-yr life) it gives only $45/share, and it swings from negative to >$100 on small changes. A 5.5x NTM EBITDA cross-check gives $78. The blend is $61, about 30% below spot. I weighed this honestly against the bull evidence: the $129B backlog, firm or rising GPU rental prices (H100 ~$2.71/hr, B200 up strongly), credit spreads that compressed in H1-2026, and sell-side targets far above spot. Valuation alone rarely forces convergence within 12 months for a 93%-vol momentum name. So the distribution is centred modestly below spot (median ~$76-80), not at my fair value. It is a mixture: 85% lognormal (median $84, sigma 0.72) plus 15% distress lognormal (median $32), roughly matching bear $35 / 30%, base $82 / 48%, bull $150 / 22%. P(>= $89) = 0.40 vs a roughly 0.45 a neutral vol-only prior would give with negative drift from dilution. Research limits: CNBC, MLQ and the Kerrisdale PDF were blocked (403). Twelve Data analyst/statistics endpoints and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits). No prediction market on CoreWeave was found. Options data was not consulted, per the brief.
